LESSON: VOLUME AND CAPACITY

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements 3.3 Area (8 lessons) • square metre (m2 ), acres, and hectares as u
Topic 3.4: Volume and Capacity
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Volume and Capacity, part of Measurements 3.3 Area (8 lessons) • square metre (m2 ), acres, and hectares as u in Grade 7 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: which they will use to work out volume ● watch videos on volume and capacity 1. Where do we use volume and capacity in daily activities?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. make a cube of sides 1 metre using locally available materials

2. discuss and work out the conversions of cm cube (cm3 ) to m cube (m3 ) and vice versa

3. collect labeled containers of different volume and capacity from the environment

4. generate conversion tables of volume and capacity

5. create models of cubes, cuboids, and cylinders

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. make a cube of sides 1 metre using locally available materials
2. discuss and work out the conversions of cm cube (cm3 ) to m cube (m3 ) and vice versa
3. collect labeled containers of different volume and capacity from the environment
4. generate conversion tables of volume and capacity
5. create models of cubes, cuboids, and cylinders

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Volume and Capacity together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and Problem-solving: as the learner creates a conversion table of units of volume.

● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner creates models of cubes and cuboids.

Values

● Responsibility: as the learner works with peers and share different tasks in making models.

● Peace: as the learner discusses and makes models for different volumes and capacities.
